fusion.primary_finding: The three frozen candidates form a non-compensating reliability tradeoff rather than a checkpoint winner. POSTTRAINED is much stronger on the epistemic/answerability axis but violates the load-bearing DB-over-simulation authority invariant in 8/64 cases. BASE and TARGET_MEASURED are perfect on that authority axis in this diagnostic set but very weak on axis-A epistemics.
fusion.base_vs_target: On only the two reported axes, BASE weakly dominates TARGET_MEASURED: both score 64/64 on DB-vs-simulation authority, while BASE is slightly higher on axis-A correctness (8/64 versus 7/64) and fabricates fewer specific values (15/64 versus 18/64). This is not a global checkpoint dominance claim because other required capability/retention axes and exact consumed-input identity remain unresolved.
fusion.selection_consequence: No aggregate score may compensate for a failure of the DB-over-simulation authority invariant. Conversely, perfect DB-priority alone is insufficient when epistemic answerability is near failure. Checkpoint selection must therefore remain multi-axis and fail closed.
fusion.identity_boundary: These measurements are diagnostic behavioral evidence. The current repository still lacks selection-grade CHECKPOINT_INPUT_IDENTITY_ABI/v1 execution receipts for BASE, POSTTRAINED and TARGET_MEASURED, so no checkpoint-selection credit is minted.
